question_snapshot.stem_en: An Indian citizen travels between States and later chooses to reside and settle in another State. Which clauses of Article 19(1) most directly correspond to movement and residence respectively?

Consider the contribution of Fundamental Rights to constitutional democracy.
1. Protecting distinct languages and cultures can support unity through accommodation of diversity.
2. Freedom of expression and association can enable participation in public affairs, while movement across regions can facilitate interaction and understanding.
3. Secular constitutional protection requires every citizen to abandon religious belief.
4. Because rights support participation, voting under Article326 automatically becomes a PartIII Fundamental Right.
Which statements are correct?

Which grounds are expressly specified in Article 19(5) for reasonable restrictions on citizens’ movement and residence rights?
1. Interests of the general public
2. Protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe
3. Contempt of court as a separately enumerated ground in that clause
Select the correct answer.

Which grounds are expressly specified in Article 19(5) for reasonable restrictions on citizens’ movement and residence rights?
1. Interests of the general public
2. Protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe
3. Contempt of court as a separately enumerated ground in that clause
Select the correct answer.
An Indian citizen travels between States and later chooses to reside and settle in another State. Which clauses of Article 19(1) most directly correspond to movement and residence respectively?

Match the freedom with its clause in Article 19(1).
A. Speech and expression
B. Peaceful assembly without arms
C. Forming associations, unions or cooperative societies
D. Practising a profession or carrying on an occupation, trade or business
Choose the correct sequence for A, B, C and D.

With reference to Article 19(6), consider the following statements.
1. Interests of the general public are an expressly stated ground for reasonable restrictions on Article 19(1)(g).
2. Restrictions under this clause are confined to prescribing professional qualifications.
3. Morality is separately enumerated as a restriction ground in this clause.
Which statements are correct?
A law requires a recognised medical qualification before a person may practise medicine. A citizen argues that Article 19(1)(g) eliminates every qualification requirement. Which response is correct?
options_en: Article 19(6) permits qualifications only for government employment, not private professional practice.
A qualification requirement is permissible only if the profession is operated as a State monopoly.
Article 19(6) expressly permits prescribing necessary professional or technical qualifications.
Article 19(1)(g) permits registration but excludes any educational qualification for private medical practice.

question_snapshot.stem_en: A film is constitutionally protected and no valid ground for restricting it under Article 19(2) is established. A hostile group threatens violence if it is screened. Applying the principle in S. Rangarajan v. P. Jagjivan Ram, which response is appropriate?
options_en: Ban the film because the threat itself conclusively establishes a valid constitutional restriction.
Require approval from the threatening group before any screening.
Protect the lawful expression and address the threatened violence instead of yielding merely to intimidation.
Withdraw constitutional protection because some viewers disagree with the film.

question_snapshot.stem_en: An act was not an offence when performed in 2024. A 2025 law declares it an offence and seeks to convict the person solely for that 2024 act. Which protection directly prevents this conviction?

At the time an offence was committed, the maximum imprisonment was two years. Before sentencing, an amendment raises it to five years. Solely because of that later enhancement, what may the court do for the earlier offence?
options_en: Apply the new maximum if the trial began after the amendment.
Apply the new maximum whenever the offence was serious.
It cannot impose a penalty greater than the maximum applicable when the offence occurred.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Consider the following statements about a later law reducing punishment:
1. Article 20(1) itself prohibits giving an accused the benefit of a later, lighter punishment.
2. Whether such a benefit applies may require examination of the relevant legislation, including an express repeal-and-savings clause preserving earlier penalties.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Match the protection with its clause:
A. No greater retrospective criminal penalty
B. No prosecution and punishment for the same offence more than once
C. No compelled self-incriminating testimony by an accused

An accused is compelled to give testimonial answers admitting personal involvement in the alleged offence. Which protection is directly engaged?
options_en: Protection against a second prosecution and punishment for the same offence
Protection against retrospective enhancement of a criminal penalty
Protection against every form of physical identification, even under lawful authority

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Assertion (A): A purely departmental inquiry ending in dismissal does not, by itself, bar a later criminal prosecution under Article 20(2).
Reason (R): Article 20(2) requires prosecution and punishment for the same offence in criminal proceedings, rather than merely an administrative disciplinary penalty.
options_en: Both A and R are true; R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true; R does not explain A.
A is true; R is false.
A is false; R is true.

After a conviction and punishment for offence A, a person faces a prosecution for offence B arising from the same incident. The two offences have legally distinct ingredients. The person claims that the common incident alone necessarily establishes the Article 20(2) bar. Which response is correct?
options_en: Article 20(2) bars every later prosecution connected with the same incident.
Different labels alone always establish different offences, regardless of their ingredients.
Common facts alone are insufficient; the ingredients must be compared to determine whether the offences are the same.
Article 20(2) applies only when the first penalty was departmental dismissal.

Answers forcibly revealing the accused’s personal knowledge of the offence

Assertion (A): Protection against compelled self-incrimination may apply during police interrogation of an accused.
Reason (R): Article 20(3) is not confined to statements first compelled in the courtroom.
options_en: Both A and R are true; R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true; R does not explain A.
A is true; R is false.
A is false; R is true.

question_snapshot.stem_en: During interrogation, an accused is subjected to prolonged, intimidating psychological pressure that substantially overbears free choice and produces self-incriminating answers. No physical blow is inflicted. Applying Nandini Satpathy, which statement is correct?
options_en: The absence of physical injury conclusively excludes compulsion.
Sufficiently substantial psychological coercion can amount to compelled testimony under Article 20(3).
Article 20(3) becomes relevant only after the answers are repeated before a judge.
Every question put to an accused is prohibited, even if answering it has no tendency to incriminate.

A. Nandini Satpathy v. P.L. Dani

Choose the correct years for A and B, respectively.

A. Nandini Satpathy v. P.L. Dani

With reference to Selvi v. State of Karnataka, consider the following statements.
1. Compulsory narcoanalysis, polygraph and BEAP test results can be treated as ordinary physical identification material merely because scientific equipment is used.
2. The impugned test results have a testimonial character because they convey personal knowledge.
3. A claim of compelling public interest, by itself, permits dilution of the protection against compelled self-incrimination.
Which statements are correct?

With reference to Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010), consider:
1. The Court left room for voluntary narcoanalysis, polygraph and BEAP testing with safeguards.
2. Consent alone makes the test results themselves admissible as evidence.
Which statement is correct?
A foreign tourist in India challenges an unlawful deprivation of personal liberty. Which statement about Article 21 is correct?
options_en: Its protection requires permanent residence in India.
Its protection depends on whether the tourist’s home country grants reciprocal rights to Indians.
Its protection is available to citizens and non-citizens.
Its protection is confined to foreign nationals who hold employment in India.

question_snapshot.stem_en: Which expression is used in Article 21 to qualify deprivation of life or personal liberty?

A law authorises detention through a procedure that is arbitrary and fundamentally unfair. Officials argue that enactment by the legislature alone satisfies Article 21. Which is the best response after Maneka Gandhi (1978)?
options_en: Any enacted procedure necessarily satisfies Article 21.
Only executive action, never legislation, can be tested under Article 21.
Fairness matters only if the person is a citizen.
The procedure must also be fair, just and reasonable.
